PullRequest.Title: agentHost: park sessions whose provider cannot vouch for them until its catalog becomes readable
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #342077, as a separate PR. There is no separate issue; it was found while investigating today's Insiders agent host logs.

## Problem

Catalog reconciliation already parks `sourceUnresolvable` sessions, but it retried `providerUnavailable` sessions on every pass. If a provider is registered but its catalog is unreadable, reconciliation opened each of its sessions' databases on every 30 s pass, indefinitely. In today's logs, the 69 older `codex` sessions in that state were re-attempted about 10 times per session per hour before Block 4a and about 80 times after it. This predates 4a, and #342077 left it in place.

## Fix

- **Parking:** `providerUnavailable` now parks a session like `sourceUnresolvable`. This applies both when the provider is unregistered (checked before any storage is opened) and when a registered provider can't vouch for the session. Parked sessions remember their provider.
- **Wake on an event, not a timer:** when a provider's catalog becomes readable, `wakeParkedProviderSessions` releases only that provider's parked sessions, and schedules a pass only if any were released. That pass re-projects them and converts their legacy chat catalogs. Provider registration, session mutations and the hourly verification still wake parked sessions as before.
- **Race:** a wake generation stops a pass from parking a session whose source it resolved just before a wake, in the same way as the existing dirty-marker check.
- **Chat moves (#342047):** parking and every wake, including the new per-provider wake, fire `onDidChangeParkedSessions`. Chat movability treats a parked legacy catalog as unverifiable, so it stays current. A loaded session never resolves `providerUnavailable` (its live summary supplies the metadata), so this doesn't block moves of open sessions.
- **Docs:** AGENTS.md describes both parking reasons and their wake signals.

## Measurement (passes every 30 s)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Unit test, 110 sessions, session DB opens in an hour | 6,000 | 110 (each session once, when it is parked), then the hourly verification's sample of 50 |
| End to end, 70 sessions, session DB opens per pass | 150 every pass | 150, then 60, then 0 |
| Converted once the catalog becomes readable (end to end) | — | 70 of 70 |

## Tests

- **New:**
  - An hour of passes over 110 sessions from two providers, with a per-provider wake and the hourly verification.
  - The wake-generation race.
  - An unregistered provider is parked without opening storage.
  - Parking and the per-provider wake fire change events for each session.
  - End to end through `AgentService` with the real database: 70 sessions are parked, then woken and converted when the catalog becomes readable.
- **Updated:** the existing tests that relied on `providerUnavailable` being retried every pass now use a failing source. The chat-move tests from #342047 call the new `_park` signature.
- **Mutations:** eight, each applied, transpiled and run against both suite files, and each killed:
  1. Don't park a resolved `providerUnavailable`.
  2. Don't park a session whose provider is unregistered.
  3. No wake when the catalog becomes readable.
  4. The provider wake releases every provider's sessions.
  5. No wake-generation guard.
  6. Schedule a pass even when nothing was woken.
  7. The provider wake isn't announced.
  8. Parking isn't announced.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`: passed.
- `npm run test-node -- --run …/agentService.test.ts --run …/agentHostCatalogReconciliationService.test.ts --run …/agentHostChatCatalogMigration.test.ts --run …/agentHostChatMovability.test.ts`: 1159 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob "**/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: 11688 passing, 14 failing. All 14 are `CopilotAgent` environment failures; the same 14 fail on unmodified main.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: 2 errors, both in `copilotSdkManagedSettings.integrationTest.ts` (`ensembleTier`). That file is untouched here, and the same 2 errors occur on unmodified `origin/main`. This change adds none.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: passed.
- Hygiene (`npm run precommit`, also run by the commit hook): passed.
- `npm run build-fast` was not run; dependency install hits an npm E401, and credentials were not changed.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Dirty provider-unavailable sessions remained eligible forever, repeating per-session database opens and source resolution every periodic pass.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Production logs showed dozens of older sessions repeatedly reopened; the representative test models 6,000 database opens per hour for 110 sessions.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Unavailable-provider rows are attempted once and excluded from normal periodic passes until a provider-readable wake or hourly verification releases them.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 671 returned providerUnavailable while leaving the row dirty, so `_listDirtySessions` selected it again on each 30-second pass and reconciliation reopened its session database. RIGHT line 704 now parks that row. The added 110-session test demonstrates the call path and multiplicity: 6,000 opens/hour before versus 110 initial opens plus bounded event/hourly retries after, with batches of 50 and concurrency 4.

Scenarios.Scenario: Periodic catalog reconciliation while a registered provider cannot read its catalog, or while a provider is unregistered
Scenarios.CriticalPath: This is background maintenance after startup/listing; it is not on an interactive critical path. Each pass must list receipts/sessions, then reconcile at most one batch. Before the PR, dirty unavailable-provider rows stayed eligible indefinitely; after the PR, their first attempt and parking must complete, while warm passes skip them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: `tryOpenDatabase(session)` opens each selected session database before source resolution for registered-but-unreadable providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold process: one open per dirty affected session, in batches of at most 50 and concurrency 4. Warm parked state: zero opens on ordinary passes. Hourly verification releases parked rows, so each can be retried once per verification cycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same unavailable dirty sessions remained eligible and were reopened every periodic pass; the representative 110-session scenario produced 6,000 opens/hour.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background I/O determines completion of the reconciliation batch but does not block interactive progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-read the central `payloadDirty` marker before recording a negative parked state, guarding concurrent mutations/wakes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One central marker read per parking attempt, bounded by 50 selected sessions per regular pass and then suppressed until wake.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider-unavailable branches returned immediately without this validation read and without caching the unavailable state, so the session was selected again indefinitely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one central read to the cold parking attempt, but enables elimination of all ordinary warm-pass session database opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve provider-side session metadata through the registered agent when the provider exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per selected session on the cold attempt; effective cardinality becomes zero on warm ordinary passes while parked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider metadata lookup was repeated whenever each dirty session returned to a later pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background source resolution gates parking or projection for that session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of dirty sessions owned by unavailable providers. The test and production context establish realistic cardinalities of roughly 70-110; batching reduces instantaneous work to 50 and concurrency to 4.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A regular pass selects at most 50 sessions and uses a shared Limiter with concurrency 4. Per-session catalog sync is additionally serialized by storage key. Passes are coalesced and observe a minimum interval; there is no unbounded Promise.all boundary burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `_parkedSessions` is an in-memory negative cache keyed by session and carrying provider. Cold restart retries each row once. Warm ordinary passes filter parked rows. Session mutation, provider registration/readability, and hourly verification invalidate it; empty/failure states are not persisted indefinitely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the dirty-list filter, local database open, batch/concurrency limits, new parking branch, and 110-session/120-pass test directly establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact filesystem and provider lookup duration varies by platform/provider, but the before/after boundary multiplicity is directly established by code and tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This scenario is a concrete repeated-I/O fix, recorded separately with the introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provider catalog transitions from unreadable to readable and wakes its parked sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider enumeration/import must finish before readability is recorded. The new provider-specific map scan and parked-session events execute synchronously at that transition; the actual re-projection is only scheduled and is off the import call's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call `provider.listChatsToMigrate()` to establish that the provider catalog is readable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider enumeration per migration attempt, independent of parked-session count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same migration/enumeration occurred, but successful readability did not release only that provider's parked reconciliation rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing provider operation gates the readability transition; the diff does not add or move it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and re-project each woken session database during scheduled reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One eventual open per woken dirty session, grouped into batches of 50 with concurrency 4; a 70-session provider takes two passes. A provider wake with no matching rows schedules no pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Those rows were already being opened on every ordinary periodic pass, including while unreadable; there was no event-triggered convergence point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the provider import critical path because `schedule()` only enqueues background reconciliation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total parked entries controls the synchronous scan; matching entries control later I/O. Realistic evidence is 55-70 matching sessions among 110 total parked sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The wake scan is single-threaded O(total parked sessions). Subsequent reconciliation remains at 50 sessions per pass and concurrency 4, with per-session key serialization. `readableTransition` makes the provider wake one-shot until readability is explicitly lost.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Readability is positively cached in `_readableProviderCatalogs`; only a false-to-true transition invokes the new provider wake. The parked cache is invalidated only for matching provider entries, and a no-match wake returns false and avoids scheduling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: transition guard, provider-specific invalidation, return-value scheduling gate, and batch limiter are explicit in the code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Providers with much larger historical catalogs could increase the linear scan/event count, but no evidence indicates a user-visible latency issue at established cardinalities.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The synchronous O(N) map scan is bounded by registered parked sessions and replaces substantially larger repeated I/O; projection remains deferred and limited.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat movability reacts when sessions are parked or released
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Parking/release fires an in-memory event synchronously. For a loaded matching session, chat movability recomputes each chat before the event returns; for the old unloaded sessions that drive this fix, `_updateSessionChats` immediately sees no state and does no work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Loaded chats in each affected session. The performance-fix scenario concerns legacy unloaded sessions, making effective chat cardinality zero there.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per event. Parking and provider-specific wake emit at most one event per affected session; the existing global hourly wake emits one `undefined` event and performs one all-loaded-session recomputation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Movability reads the parked map directly; no stale cache or repeated scheduled work is introduced. Per-provider release deletes entries before firing, so consumers observe authoritative state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous call path and no-op behavior on unloaded sessions; low prevalence for large loaded parked sets is not used as a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A provider could theoretically have many loaded sessions/chats, but loaded sessions resolve from live summaries and are not expected to enter the provider-unavailable parked state; no realistic hot-path regression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous-UI regression. The event fan-out is necessary, session-scoped, and effectively empty for the realistic affected population.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. The PR fixes a shipped repeated-I/O mechanism by negatively caching unavailable-provider sessions, with bounded provider/hourly invalidation, batch size 50, and concurrency 4. No high-confidence performance regression was introduced; the new synchronous wake scan/events are bounded and the expensive re-projection remains scheduled off the provider-readability critical path.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
